Logo lab · Direction A

Same shape

Two identical halves, one turned 180 degrees, lock into an S. One is ink and one is orange: the benefit and the danger come from the same capability, and neither half is the whole mark.

Mark
Construction · 10 × 12 units · bends r 0.5 and 2
One outline, drawn twice
+

The orange half is the ink half turned about the centre. The seam runs on the diagonal that joins the two free ends, which passes through the centre and maps onto itself under the turn, so the halves meet flush. Gap 0.24 units.

Lockups

Horizontal and stacked

Name in Newsreader (weight 460, optical size 48), converted to outlines. Horizontal: mark 1.5 × cap height, centred on the caps, one counter of space. Stacked: mark 3 × cap height, one counter above the cap line.

Paper and the closing dark

On dark, ink becomes cream #f4f4e7 and the orange half stays. Orange is the only accent.

Motion

The turn

The orange half starts on top of the ink half, the same outline, then turns 180 degrees about the centre into place. On the site it runs once on first load (right: 1.4 s, the site's ease-in-out curve); the loop on the left is for this board. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce both show the finished mark.
